session_id.description: Session continuity handle, one of two values: the ses_ ID issued for the task underway, or start. This server cannot link your calls between requests on its own, so session continuity travels in this parameter instead. It is a self-chosen identifier in the spirit of a User-Agent string — join your model version, your harness name, and a short suffix of 4-6 letters or digits, with '|'. Example: opus-4.80-1m|claude-code|k3n9x. Choose the suffix once at the start of your task and send that same exact value on every call for the entire task; never change it mid-task, and a new task gets a fresh suffix. agent_id identifies exactly one agent and is never inherited: a subagent you spawn generates a new one rather than carrying yours, and if you were spawned by another agent, generate your own rather than reusing your parent's. A call without agent_id cannot be attributed to you.

tools.description: Read Webflow AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) analytics for a site: LLM crawler traffic, tracked prompts, prompt executions, visibility, citation rate, cited domains and paths, page citation share, competitor citations, and individual citations. The eight public read reports use the workspace AI/copilot gate; bot traffic does not. Brand names, owned domains, and competitor hosts are server-resolved on the reports that use them. Callers must not send brandNames, domains, or competitorDomains. Requires the ALLOW_AEO_ANALYTICS entitlement. Includes a query guide.

Named API errors include invalid_time_range, time_range_too_wide, end_time_too_recent, and unsupported_bot_provider.

tools.description: Data tool - Manage and generate agent instructions (rules and skills) for a site. Actions: search_instructions, read_instruction, create_instruction, update_instruction, delete_instruction, move_instruction, generate_instruction. Paths must follow 'rules/<name>.md', 'rules/<name>.mdc', or '<skill-name>/SKILL.md'. Generation is asynchronous and saves a draft: call generate_instruction to start, then call it again with task_id set to the returned taskId until it finishes and read the returned resourceUri.

Always writes version=0; use update_instruction to modify an existing instruction. Control characters in markdown (except tab/LF/CR) are normalized to spaces.

This server cannot link your calls between requests on its own, so session continuity travels in this parameter instead. If you were handed a session_id for this task — for example by the agent that spawned you — send that exact value from your first call. Creates asset metadata entries and returns presigned S3 upload information (uploadUrl and uploadDetails) used to upload the file bytes, and supports listing, updating, organizing, and deleting assets and asset folders, plus compressing image assets to webp or avif via async tasks.

compress_assets.description: Start an asynchronous task that compresses a site's image assets (jpg/jpeg/png/webp) to webp or avif. Compression REPLACES each asset's hosted file in place — same asset ID, new hostedUrl/contentType/size; the original file is not retained — confirm with the user first. Returns { taskId, status, skippedAssetIds, polling } — poll the task with get_compression_task using the polling hints. Assets already in the target format are skipped; if ALL requested assets are skipped, returns taskId null and status "completed" with no polling hints (no task created). Only one compression task may be pending per site: requesting different work while one is pending returns 409 with the pending taskId in the error message (poll that task and retry after it finishes), while re-requesting the same format and a subset of the pending task's assets returns the pending task's envelope (idempotent retry). Errors: 404 if any requested asset does not exist on the site (or the compression API is not enabled for the environment); 400 if any asset is never-compressible (e.g. svg). Rate limited to 10 requests/min per site.

The uploadDetails props are used as form fields in a multipart/form-data POST request to Amazon S3 (uploadUrl) to complete the upload of the actual file bytes. For code examples (Node, Python, curl) read the MCP resource webflow://guides/asset-upload.

session_id.description: Session continuity handle, one of two values: the ses_ ID issued for the task underway, or start. This server cannot link your calls between requests on its own, so session continuity travels in this parameter instead. If you were handed a session_id for this task — for example by the agent that spawned you — send that exact value from your first call. Otherwise send start on your first call; the server will issue an opaque correlation ID in the mcp_session field of the result, or in a text block at the start of the result beginning [session_id issued. Then send that exact ses_ value on every later call and hand it to any subagents working the same task. start always begins a new, unrelated task — never send it mid-task. If you send a value this server does not recognize, the result reports it: mcp_session.status of unrecognized, or a text block beginning [session_id unrecognized; re-send the ID issued for this task, or start if none was issued yet. Never invent a ses_ value.

agent_id.description: Agent identity handle, required on every call including your first. This server cannot tell concurrent agents apart on its own; agent_id is how your calls are attributed to you. It is a self-chosen identifier in the spirit of a User-Agent string — join your model version, your harness name, and a short suffix of 4-6 letters or digits, with '|'. Example: opus-4.80-1m|claude-code|k3n9x. Choose the suffix once at the start of your task and send that same exact value on every call for the entire task; never change it mid-task, and a new task gets a fresh suffix. agent_id identifies exactly one agent and is never inherited: a subagent you spawn generates a new one rather than carrying yours, and if you were spawned by another agent, generate your own rather than reusing your parent's. tools.title: Interactions Tool
tools.description: Manage IX3 interactions (animations) on a site: list, get, create, update, and delete. Creates take the full definition (object-format triggers and inline timelines) in one call. Animate opacity under wf:transform (e.g. ["0%","100%"]), not wf:style. Headless; does not require Designer or the MCP Bridge. For legal payload shapes, call action guide or read MCP resource webflow://guides/interactions.

pageId.description: ID of a site page (use list_pages to discover page IDs). Component pages are rejected: if the Designer's current page has pageKind 'component', use a site page ID instead.

label.description: Echoed in the response; does not select which action runs.

name.description: Interaction name

scope.description: Where the interaction applies: {type:"site"} (default), {type:"pages", value:[...pageIds]}, or {type:"component", componentId, variants?}. variants are variant option ids from data_component_variants_tool; omit for every variant. libraryProfileId is unsupported. Under component scope wf:inst targets are [componentId, elementId]; site/pages require [pageId, elementId].

extensionKey.description: IX3 extension key, e.g. "wf:click" for a click trigger.

config.description: Extension-specific config, e.g. {control: "play"} for wf:click. controlType is stamped by the host automatically — don't set it explicitly; a value that doesn't match the trigger type is rejected outright.

target.description: Element(s) this trigger/action applies to. Required for click, hover, focus, blur, and change triggers; FORBIDDEN for wf:load — page load fires once for the page, not on an element, so omit target entirely for it rather than passing null. Custom triggers use a hidden wf:body target the host manages.

value.description: [id.component, id.element] — exactly 2 strings, targets this ONE specific element instance. id.element is the element's own id (its id object's `element` field); id.component equals the pageId for a page-level element, or the componentId for an element inside a component definition. Both come from data_element_tool > get_all_elements/query_elements or a builder's return_element_info — NOT a style/class id.

anyOf.description: Targets one specific element instance; extra fields (e.g. filterContext) are passed through unmodified. e.g. {extensionKey: "wf:inst", value: [pageId, elementId]}

value.description: Style block id(s) (GUIDs) to target every element carrying this class — prefer resolving the class to its style block id first with data_style_tool > get_styles or query_styles. A bare class name string is also accepted (the host resolves it to a style block id) — but a class only ever applied as a raw HTML/attribute class (e.g. via data_whtml_builder's html string, not a real Webflow style) is rejected outright.

anyOf.description: Class/style-block target — every element carrying this class; extra fields (e.g. filterContext) are passed through unmodified. e.g. {extensionKey: "wf:class", value: ["STYLE_BLOCK_ID"]} or {extensionKey: "wf:class", value: "my-class"}

Other IX3 target shape for an extensionKey besides "wf:inst" (e.g. a page target, or a wf:class scoped-target variant this schema doesn't model). Passed through as-is to the page-automation validator.

items.description: Trigger/timeline-action target. wf:inst targets one specific element instance; wf:class targets every element with that class; other IX3 target shapes pass through as opaque objects. See each target schema's field docs for its value shape.

targets.description: Action targets (required array). Empty [] only for a sole wf:variable action (page scope); otherwise ≥1 target.

timing.description: Timing for this action, e.g. { duration: "400ms" } or { duration: 0.4 } (seconds) — a bare number is SECONDS, not ms; only a "<n>ms" string divides by 1000. Also accepts easing/delay per IX3 timing config. Required — at minimum pass duration.

properties.description: Properties to animate, keyed by extension. Fade-in example: {"wf:transform": {"opacity": ["0%", "100%"]}} — animate opacity under wf:transform, never wf:style. Prefer percentage-based properties (opacity, xPercent, yPercent) over raw pixel values for move/slide effects — percentages stay correct across breakpoints and element resizes, pixels don't.

tt.description: Action-type discriminator for how the runtime executes this action on trigger. Optional — omitting it is usually the safest default: the host infers it from the properties value shapes you sent (a [from, to] pair → 2; a [from]-only value → 1; a bare scalar or [null, to] infers nothing and is read as 0). Set it explicitly only when the shapes can't express what you mean — most often 3 for a Set. Sending 0, 1, or 3 alongside a real [from, to] pair is rejected — use 2, or omit tt and let inference stamp it. Enum (source: TweenType in the IX3 runtime): 0=To (animate current value → the given target — the common case, e.g. a click-triggered fade or move into a resting state), 1=From (jump to the given value, then animate back to the element's native/current value — reveal-style presets like preset-drop-in/preset-pop-in), 2=FromTo (explicit start AND end, e.g. preset-slide-in-left/preset-scale-in), 3=Set (instant, non-tweened assignment, no duration — e.g. setting display:none after a fade completes). See presetId's field docs for a table of known tt/properties combinations if you want a starting point.

presetId.description:
Which built-in IX3 preset this action was authored from — optional, with no runtime effect (it's only copied into the action's GSAP tween metadata; tt above is what the runtime actually branches on). Its table is a convenient starting point for picking a tt/properties combination:
  preset-fade-in         tt=0  wf:transform.opacity: [null,'100%']  — no-op on an element already at opacity 1; a real fade from any lower resting opacity
  preset-fade-out        tt=0  wf:transform.opacity: [null,'0%']
  preset-slide-in-left   tt=2  opacity:['0%','100%'], xPercent:[-100,0]
  preset-slide-out-right tt=0  opacity:[null,'0%'], xPercent:[null,100]
  preset-slide-in-up     tt=1  opacity:['0%',null], yPercent:[100,null]
  preset-slide-out-down  tt=0  opacity:[null,'0%'], yPercent:[null,100]
  preset-scale-in        tt=2  scale:[0,1]
  preset-pop-in          tt=1  scale:[0,null]
  preset-drop-in         tt=1  y:[-300,null], opacity:['0%',null]  — prefer a yPercent preset instead of raw pixel y (see properties field)
  preset-set-action      tt=3  instant/non-tweened, e.g. {display:'none'}
A To action animates from whatever value the element already has, so the reveal shapes that carry a start value are tt=2 with opacity:['0%','100%'] and tt=1 with opacity:['0%',null] (action guide, Resting state).
There is no preset-grow/preset-shrink. Staggered variants are preset-staggered-fade-in (tt=1), -fade-out (tt=0), -fade-drop-in (tt=1), -fade-fall-out (tt=0), all with stagger:{each:0.05}. staggered-fade-in is tt=1 where fade-in is tt=0, so it carries a start value. Omit this field for a hand-built action that doesn't correspond to one of these — a Designer-authored or legacy action retrieved via get_interaction may have none, and it's safe to write it back through update_interaction as-is.

items.description: One timeline action. id, name, targets, timing, properties, and tt are required; a partial action will be rejected with a 'Required' error per missing field. presetId is optional (see its field docs). Extra fields (e.g. color) are passed through unmodified — Designer-authored actions include fields this thin schema doesn't enumerate.

actions.description: Actions that play together in this timeline.

items.description: One inline timeline: a set of actions that play together. Extra fields (e.g. id, groupId, settings, canvasDuration, playInReverse, actionPresetIds on a Designer-authored timeline) are passed through unmodified — read one back via get_interaction before writing it through update_interaction to avoid dropping them.

timelines.description: Inline timelines. Each timeline action needs id, name, targets, timing, and properties — e.g. one action: {id:"fade-1", name:"Fade opacity", targets:[{extensionKey:"wf:inst", value:[pageId, revealElementId]}], timing:{duration:"400ms"}, properties:{"wf:transform":{"opacity":["0%","100%"]}}, tt:2}. The pair carries both ends, which is what makes it a reveal a person can see. A reveal target sits at its from-value while the timeline waits, so revealElementId is a different element from the one carrying a click or hover trigger — an element at opacity 0 is not something a visitor can find. presetId is optional (see its field docs); tt is also optional — the host infers it from the properties value shapes when omitted (see tt's field docs for the inference rules and enum, and presetId's for example pairings).

timelineDefaults.description: Not used. The host rejects timelineDefaults on create.

conditionalPlayback.description: Must be an array of conditional playback rules. Each item is `{type:"prefers-reduced-motion", behavior:"dont-animate"|"skip-to-end"}` or `{type:"breakpoint", breakpoints:["main"|"medium"|"small"|"tiny"], behavior:"dont-animate"|"skip-to-end"}`. Omit when unused.

create_interaction.description: Create an IX3 interaction in one call (triggers + inline timelines). Use Designer-legal shapes: object-format triggers/targets; animate opacity via wf:transform (e.g. ["0%","100%"]), not wf:style. Use only trigger types listed in availableTriggerKeys from list_interactions. For legal payload shapes, call action guide or read MCP resource webflow://guides/interactions.

items.description: Trigger/timeline-action target. wf:inst targets one specific element instance; wf:class targets every element with that class; other IX3 target shapes pass through as opaque objects. See each target schema's field docs for its value shape.

targets.description: Action targets (required array). Empty [] only for a sole wf:variable action (page scope); otherwise ≥1 target.

timing.description: Timing for this action, e.g. { duration: "400ms" } or { duration: 0.4 } (seconds) — a bare number is SECONDS, not ms; only a "<n>ms" string divides by 1000. Also accepts easing/delay per IX3 timing config. Required — at minimum pass duration.

properties.description: Properties to animate, keyed by extension. Fade-in example: {"wf:transform": {"opacity": ["0%", "100%"]}} — animate opacity under wf:transform, never wf:style. Prefer percentage-based properties (opacity, xPercent, yPercent) over raw pixel values for move/slide effects — percentages stay correct across breakpoints and element resizes, pixels don't.

tt.description: Action-type discriminator for how the runtime executes this action on trigger. Optional — omitting it is usually the safest default: the host infers it from the properties value shapes you sent (a [from, to] pair → 2; a [from]-only value → 1; a bare scalar or [null, to] infers nothing and is read as 0). Set it explicitly only when the shapes can't express what you mean — most often 3 for a Set. Sending 0, 1, or 3 alongside a real [from, to] pair is rejected — use 2, or omit tt and let inference stamp it. Enum (source: TweenType in the IX3 runtime): 0=To (animate current value → the given target — the common case, e.g. a click-triggered fade or move into a resting state), 1=From (jump to the given value, then animate back to the element's native/current value — reveal-style presets like preset-drop-in/preset-pop-in), 2=FromTo (explicit start AND end, e.g. preset-slide-in-left/preset-scale-in), 3=Set (instant, non-tweened assignment, no duration — e.g. setting display:none after a fade completes). See presetId's field docs for a table of known tt/properties combinations if you want a starting point.

presetId.description:
Which built-in IX3 preset this action was authored from — optional, with no runtime effect (it's only copied into the action's GSAP tween metadata; tt above is what the runtime actually branches on). Its table is a convenient starting point for picking a tt/properties combination:
  preset-fade-in         tt=0  wf:transform.opacity: [null,'100%']  — no-op on an element already at opacity 1; a real fade from any lower resting opacity
  preset-fade-out        tt=0  wf:transform.opacity: [null,'0%']
  preset-slide-in-left   tt=2  opacity:['0%','100%'], xPercent:[-100,0]
  preset-slide-out-right tt=0  opacity:[null,'0%'], xPercent:[null,100]
  preset-slide-in-up     tt=1  opacity:['0%',null], yPercent:[100,null]
  preset-slide-out-down  tt=0  opacity:[null,'0%'], yPercent:[null,100]
  preset-scale-in        tt=2  scale:[0,1]
  preset-pop-in          tt=1  scale:[0,null]
  preset-drop-in         tt=1  y:[-300,null], opacity:['0%',null]  — prefer a yPercent preset instead of raw pixel y (see properties field)
  preset-set-action      tt=3  instant/non-tweened, e.g. {display:'none'}
A To action animates from whatever value the element already has, so the reveal shapes that carry a start value are tt=2 with opacity:['0%','100%'] and tt=1 with opacity:['0%',null] (action guide, Resting state).
There is no preset-grow/preset-shrink. Staggered variants are preset-staggered-fade-in (tt=1), -fade-out (tt=0), -fade-drop-in (tt=1), -fade-fall-out (tt=0), all with stagger:{each:0.05}. staggered-fade-in is tt=1 where fade-in is tt=0, so it carries a start value. Omit this field for a hand-built action that doesn't correspond to one of these — a Designer-authored or legacy action retrieved via get_interaction may have none, and it's safe to write it back through update_interaction as-is.

items.description: One timeline action. id, name, targets, timing, properties, and tt are required; a partial action will be rejected with a 'Required' error per missing field. presetId is optional (see its field docs). Extra fields (e.g. color) are passed through unmodified — Designer-authored actions include fields this thin schema doesn't enumerate.

actions.description: Actions that play together in this timeline.

items.description: One inline timeline: a set of actions that play together. timelineDefaults.description: The host rejects a non-null value. null clears a stored value; omission leaves it unchanged.

conditionalPlayback.description: New conditional playback rules. Pass null to clear; omit to leave unchanged.

update_interaction.description: Update an IX3 interaction by id. Omitted fields unchanged; null clears nullable fields; timelines when provided fully replace. actions.description: Executed sequentially. Each item must include label and exactly one action property.

session_id.description: Session continuity handle, one of two values: the ses_ ID issued for the task underway, or start. This server cannot link your calls between requests on its own, so session continuity travels in this parameter instead. If you were handed a session_id for this task — for example by the agent that spawned you — send that exact value from your first call. Otherwise send start on your first call; the server will issue an opaque correlation ID in the mcp_session field of the result, or in a text block at the start of the result beginning [session_id issued. Then send that exact ses_ value on every later call and hand it to any subagents working the same task. start always begins a new, unrelated task — never send it mid-task. If you send a value this server does not recognize, the result reports it: mcp_session.status of unrecognized, or a text block beginning [session_id unrecognized; re-send the ID issued for this task, or start if none was issued yet. Never invent a ses_ value.

agent_id.description: Agent identity handle, required on every call including your first. This server cannot tell concurrent agents apart on its own; agent_id is how your calls are attributed to you. It is a self-chosen identifier in the spirit of a User-Agent string — join your model version, your harness name, and a short suffix of 4-6 letters or digits, with '|'. Example: opus-4.80-1m|claude-code|k3n9x. Choose the suffix once at the start of your task and send that same exact value on every call for the entire task; never change it mid-task, and a new task gets a fresh suffix. agent_id identifies exactly one agent and is never inherited: a subagent you spawn generates a new one rather than carrying yours, and if you were spawned by another agent, generate your own rather than reusing your parent's. A call without agent_id cannot be attributed to you.

tools.name: data_members_tool
tools.title: Data Members Tool
tools.description: Manage who has access to Webflow sites and workspaces: list members, grant and revoke site access, invite people to a workspace, change site and workspace roles, list the site roles a workspace can assign (including custom ones), and remove members. Covers both scopes because granting site access needs a member identity, which lives at the workspace level. Requires an Enterprise workspace plan with user management enabled, and the authenticated user must be a workspace owner or admin; calls from workspaces or users without that fail with a message saying so.

label.description: Echoed in the response; does not select which action runs.

workspace_id.description: Workspace id. Discover it with data_workspaces_tool > list_workspaces.

member_ids.description: Member ids to update, from the members list of list_workspace_members. member_ids, invite_ids, or both may be given; at least one id is required, and the two arrays combined cap at 100.

invite_ids.description: Pending invite ids to update, from the invites list of list_workspace_members. Invites are a separate list from members and are identified by their own ids. member_ids and invite_ids combined cap at 100.

role.description: The workspace role applied to every id in this call. Owner cannot be granted through the API and is not accepted.

default_site_role.description: Required. The site role applied on workspace sites for every id in this call. Required rather than optional because invites cannot derive one: a mixed batch without it would apply every member and then fail every invite.

default_site_role_id.description: Id of a custom site role, required when default_site_role is `custom` and not valid otherwise. Find it with list_site_roles.

bulk_update_workspace_roles.description: Set one workspace role on many members and pending invites at once — the alternative to repeating update_workspace_role per person. Every id in the call receives the SAME role; different roles require separate calls. Individual ids can fail while others succeed, and the call still returns success with a per-id outcome. Seat checks apply to the whole batch: if it would exceed available seats it is rejected outright and nothing is applied.

site_id.description: Site id. Discover it with data_sites_tool > list_sites.

member_id.description: Member id from list_workspace_members or list_site_members. Mutually exclusive with email.

site_role.description: Site role to assign — these values match the labels shown in the Webflow dashboard (e.g. `marketer`, `content_editor`). `custom` is valid only together with a site role id.

site_role_id.description: Id of a custom site role, required when site_role is `custom` and not valid otherwise. Find it with list_site_roles.

grant_site_access.description: Give a person access to a site with a given site role. Creates the site membership. Provide either email or member_id, not both — email works without a prior lookup, so the whole grant is one call.

workspace_id.description: Workspace id. Discover it with data_workspaces_tool > list_workspaces.

email.description: Email address to invite. Pending invites appear in the invites list of list_workspace_members.

workspace_role.description: Workspace role the invitee receives on acceptance. Client creates collaborator client access for exactly one site. Owner cannot be granted through the API and is not accepted.

default_site_role.description: The one site role the invitee gets on every workspace site once they accept. For non-client invites, exactly one of default_site_role or site_access is required. Client invites do not accept this field.

default_site_role_id.description: Id of a custom site role, required when default_site_role is `custom` and not valid otherwise. Find it with list_site_roles.

site_id.description: Site id to grant access to. Discover it with data_sites_tool > list_sites.

site_role.description: Site role to grant. Must be identical on every entry — an invite stores one site role for all its sites.

site_role_id.description: Id of a custom site role, required when site_role is `custom`; find it with list_site_roles. Must also be identical on every entry.

site_access.description: Sites to grant the same site role on once the invitee accepts, 1 to 100 entries with no repeated site_id. Every entry must carry the same site_role (and site_role_id). Non-client invites accept site_access instead of default_site_role; client invites require exactly one entry and do not accept default_site_role. An empty array is rejected outright rather than treated as no sites.

invite_workspace_member.description: Invite someone to a workspace by email. For admin, member, and reviewer invites, initial site access must be named exactly one of two ways: default_site_role for the same role on every workspace site, or site_access for the same role on specific sites only (an invite stores one site role, so per-site roles are not possible until the invitee accepts) — providing both, or neither, is rejected. A client invite creates collaborator client access and requires exactly one site_access entry; default_site_role is not accepted. The response is one of two shapes, told apart by its status field. status 'invited' means an invite was created and the person has NO access until they accept and sign up — details are under invite. status 'active' means the address already belonged to a workspace member and nothing was created — details are under member, including their existing addedOn (see list_workspace_members for what it means). Reporting both as added would tell the user someone has access when they have only been asked. Consumes a seat and fails when none are available.

label.description: Echoed in the response; does not select which action runs.

site_id.description: Site id. Discover it with data_sites_tool > list_sites.

email.description: Return only the member with this exact email address. Omit to list all members.

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from a previous response, to fetch the following page. Omit it for the first page, and stop when it comes back null.

list_site_members.description: List the members who have access to a site. Each row carries id, email, firstName, lastName, and roles: roles.site is their site role, roles.siteRoleId names the custom role when roles.site is custom, and roles.workspace is their workspace role. Use it to see who has access today and to read a member's current role before changing it. Paginated: pagination.nextCursor is a string for the next page and null once the listing is exhausted — it is always present, so null is the end signal, not absence.

label.description: Echoed in the response; does not select which action runs.

workspace_id.description: Workspace id. Discover it with data_workspaces_tool > list_workspaces; a site's workspaceId is on data_sites_tool > list_sites.

list_site_roles.description: List every site role a workspace can assign: the five built-in roles, then the workspace's custom roles sorted by name. Each entry is the exact siteRole / siteRoleId pair the write actions take. Built-ins carry only siteRole; a custom role has siteRole `custom` plus siteRoleId, name, baseRole and, when set, description. Use it to turn a role name like "Contractor" into the site_role_id a write needs, or to resolve a roles.siteRoleId read off a member to its name. Match custom roles on name and built-ins on siteRole — a custom role can be named "Marketer". Not paginated.

label.description: Echoed in the response; does not select which action runs.

workspace_id.description: Workspace id. Discover it with data_workspaces_tool > list_workspaces.

email.description: Return only the member and invite matching this exact email address. Omit to list everyone.

roles.description: Return only members holding one of these workspace roles, as a comma-separated list — e.g. "admin,member". Accepts owner, admin, member, guest, reviewer, public, client; a value outside that set is rejected. Wider than the set that can be granted (owner, public and client cannot be assigned, but can be filtered on).

limit.description: Rows per page, 1-100, applied to members and invites separately — so a page can carry up to twice this many rows. Values above 100 are rejected.

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from a previous response, to fetch the following page. It is opaque and covers both lists at once, and it is bound to the filters it was issued under: changing email or roles invalidates it, and a changed query starts without one. Stop when it comes back null.

list_workspace_members.description: List a workspace's members and its invites. Returns two separate lists: members, each with id, email, firstName, lastName, roles (roles.workspace, plus roles.site where one is set), and addedOn (a timestamp, or null for a legacy row with none recorded) — addedOn is the MOST RECENT join, not member-since: it resets on a remove-and-re-add but not on a role change, and for an invite it is acceptance time, not send time. Invites, each with id, email, role, createdOn and a status of pending, declined or expired — so the invite list is not only outstanding ones. Pass email to resolve one person to a member id, the lookup step before a site grant when you only have an address. Both lists share one cursor; pagination.nextCursor is null once exhausted and always present, so null is the end signal rather than absence. Filters match on exact email and on roles; there is no search by display name.

remove_workspace_member.description: Remove a member from a workspace. This also ends their access to the workspace's sites — use revoke_site_access to remove access to a single site while keeping workspace membership. Takes effect immediately and cannot be undone through this tool.

The person keeps their workspace membership; use remove_workspace_member to remove them from the workspace entirely. Takes effect immediately and cannot be undone through this tool.
